statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-2003 (PostgreSQL oidvector discloses a few bytes of memory) is fixed upstream in PostgreSQL 17.8: https://www.postgresql.org/support/security/CVE-2026-2003/ lists 17.8 as the fixed release for major version 17, and the 17.8 release notes, https://www.postgresql.org/docs/release/17.8/, include it. Alpine's postgresql17 17.8-r0 is the upgrade to upstream 17.8 and lists CVE-2026-2003 under its secfixes: https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/ce22298320177ae25085d86fbf3b4fc1150c16a2/main/postgresql17/APKBUILD. The DHI postgresql17 packages for Alpine 3.23 are built from Alpine's postgresql17 APKBUILD at the aports revision for each package version (the current revision is linked above) and the upstream source release of the same version, and the postgres server binary in every published build (17.7-r0, 17.8-r0, 17.9-r0, 17.10-r0, 17.11-r0 and 17.12-r0), on both x86_64 and aarch64, reports the matching PostgreSQL 17 release. The affected code is in the PostgreSQL server, which ships in the postgresql17 package. The earlier published build for Alpine 3.23 (17.7-r0) is built from an earlier upstream release and its server binary reports that older version, and Alpine applies no backport of this fix to it, so it is recorded as affected; 17.8-r0 and later carry the fix.
